summary: Frontend-only e2e test of CYBER HQ theatrical classroom game. Verified full flow: launcher -> command-center -> Mission 1 Identity (Trust warning w/ Try Again + Don't Trust scan + passed w/ Key #1 + Cyber Rule #1) -> Mission 2 Cryptography (KHOOR wheel rotate right x3 -> HELLO, cipher-wrong at shift 0, ArrowLeft/Right keys work, no auto-advance, presenter puzzles easy=FDW->CAT and challenge=VHFUHW->SECRET all solvable at shift 3) -> Mission 3 Integrity (original 7A-91-C4-22/BLUE, press 'g' triggers intercept -> tampered 3F-82-B9-17/RED, investigate -> compare-view -> hash-mismatch, RED shows gentle 'HMM — THE ORIGINAL SAID BLUE' retry w/o advancing, BLUE advances to integrity-verified with 3 open locks + Final Key) -> Finale (activate-defense-btn -> verify/removing/plead/access-denied/mission-complete/user-blocked/career-conclusion all sequential -> meet-team -> welcome-cyber-team -> victory-reset returns to secure command-center). Global shortcuts 1/2/3/r/p/g/a/h/f all functional, no page scrolling at 1920x1080, no 'WRONG' shaming on Trust path. Educational integrity confirmed (BLUE is correct answer, gentle re-try messaging).
critical_code_review_comments: Mission3Integrity uses global 'g' keydown listener during original stage that will double-fire alongside App-level 'g' handler (which also dispatches GLITCH effect) — currently harmless because both effects are desired, but worth noting.

Mission1 scan uses setInterval + setTimeout without checking unmount, but return cleanup only clears interval; the trailing setTimeout(1400) that calls onSolved+setStage('passed') could fire after unmount if user presses '1'/'r' during scan. Consider tracking timeout id and clearing on cleanup.

Mission2 keyboard ArrowLeft/Right listener uses stale closure of rotate() — currently works because rotate is defined in render scope, but the eslint-disable suggests future maintenance risk; acceptable for now.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All flows tested via keyboard shortcuts and data-testids. Mission 3 original message uses TypeLines typewriter (~2s) — wait 2.5s before asserting on text. Finale is ~20s cinematic; use wait_for_selector w/ ~15s timeout per stage. When testing standalone missions after 'r' reset, HUD locks won't be green (expected, that's the mission-completion state, not visited state).
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found. Initial mission3 assertion failure in first run was due to reading original-message text before typewriter finished; retest with proper wait passed.
